title: Proposal for Compulsory Law, Social Norms and Security Awareness Courses for Foreigners Working or Residing in Singapore
what_it_is: Proposal for Compulsory Law, Social Norms and Security Awareness Courses for Foreigners Working or Residing in Singapore

sections.label: Onboarding programmes for foreign workers
sections.summary: New Work Permit holders receive guidebooks, and FDWs and some foreign workers attend compulsory programmes covering Singapore laws and social norms.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mrs Josephine Teo) (for the Prime Minister)
sentences.text: For example, upon their arrival in Singapore, all new Work Permit holders receive guidebooks that cover Singapore laws, employment regulations and social norms.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mrs Josephine Teo) (for the Prime Minister)
sentences.text: In addition, all new foreign domestic workers (FDWs) attend a Settling-in Programme, and new foreign workers from the Construction, Marine, Process and Metalworking sectors attend Safety Orientation Courses, both of which cover aspects of Singapore laws and our social norms.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mrs Josephine Teo) (for the Prime Minister)
sentences.text: Annually, these compulsory programmes cover close to two-thirds of all new Work Permit holders coming to Singapore.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mrs Josephine Teo) (for the Prime Minister)
sentences.text: In addition, the National Integration Council also partners the Singapore National Employers Federation (SNEF) to offer the Workplace Integration Programme which provides training on supervising multicultural teams.

sections.label: Integration needs continued support
sections.summary: Onboarding programmes help foreigners adjust, but integration takes time and needs continued support from Singaporeans and foreigners to foster social cohesion.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mrs Josephine Teo) (for the Prime Minister)
sentences.text: The various onboarding programmes have helped foreigners better understand and adjust to living in a multicultural, multiracial and multi-religious Singapore.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mrs Josephine Teo) (for the Prime Minister)
sentences.text: However, integration takes time and cannot be achieved through one-off programmes.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mrs Josephine Teo) (for the Prime Minister)
sentences.text: We will need the continued support of Singaporeans and foreigners across all parts of society to work together to foster social cohesion and integration.
